The AI Builder's Toolbox

What to reach for, by the thing you're actually trying to do.

149 tools across 19 domains. A ★ means I've actually used it, not just bookmarked it. Every link was checked on 2026-08-13.

Start Here

If you only open six links, open these.

  • ★ Claude Code — The terminal coding agent everything else on this page plugs into.
  • ★ Claude Docs / API — Model IDs, pricing, prompt caching, tool use — the primary source, not a blog post.
  • ★ anthropics/skills — Official Agent Skills repo. Read one SKILL.md and you'll understand the whole format.
  • anthropics/claude-plugins-official — Anthropic-curated plugin directory. Safest place to install from first.
  • hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code — The big hand-picked community list. Go here when this page doesn't have it.
  • ★ Model Context Protocol — The spec behind MCP servers. Worth 20 minutes before you install your first one.

Frontend & Design

Stopping your agent from producing generic purple-gradient slop.

  • ★ pbakaus/impeccable — A design language you drop in so the agent stops defaulting to bootstrap-brain.
  • ★ Leonxlnx/taste-skill — Gives the model actual taste. The anti-slop skill people mean when they say anti-slop.
  • Nutlope/hallmark — Same job as the two above, different opinion. Works in Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
  • ★ VoltAgent/awesome-design-md — DESIGN.md files reverse-engineered from real brand systems. Drop one in your repo.
  • google-labs-code/design.md — The actual spec for describing a visual identity to a coding agent.
  • ★ 21st.dev — Component marketplace + MCP so the agent can pull real UI instead of inventing it.
  • ★ shadcn/ui — The component library most agent-generated React lands on. Know it.
  • shadcn/improve — Use your best model to audit the codebase, then let a cheap model execute the plan.
  • ★ nexu-io/open-design — Local-first desktop app; open-source take on Claude Design.
  • ★ facebook/astryx — Open-source design system built to be driven by an agent.
  • ★ alchaincyf/huashu-design — HTML-native design skill — good when you want markup, not a framework.
  • nexu-io/html-anything — Agentic HTML editor. Agent writes the markup, you ship it.
  • ★ Tailwind CSS — Assume every agent already knows it. Fight this and you'll lose.
  • oil-oil/oil-motion — Smooth, responsive web animations without hand-rolling easing curves.
  • Jakubantalik/thinking-orbs — Loading indicators built specifically for AI/agent UIs. Small but you'll want it.
  • ★ Figma — Still where the design actually gets decided before code touches it.

Diagrams & Visual Explainers

For when the answer is a picture, not a paragraph.

  • cathrynlavery/diagram-design — 29 editorial diagram types as clean HTML+SVG. No Mermaid look, no drop shadows.
  • tt-a1i/archify — Architecture, sequence, data-flow and lifecycle diagrams that are actually verifiable.
  • coleam00/excalidraw-diagram-skill — Makes any coding agent produce real Excalidraw files.
  • yizhiyanhua-ai/fireworks-tech-graph — Natural language in, production-quality SVG/PNG technical diagrams out.
  • ★ Excalidraw — The hand-drawn whiteboard. Fastest path from head to shareable picture.
  • ★ Mermaid — Diagrams as text. Renders natively in GitHub and most docs tools.

Context & Token Management

The single biggest lever on cost and on whether long sessions stay coherent.

  • ★ JuliusBrussee/caveman — "Why use many token when few token do trick." Cuts roughly 65% of tokens.
  • ★ DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes the agent think like the laziest senior dev alive. Best code is the code you don't write.
  • Mibayy/token-savior — MCP server that held 97.9% on a real coding benchmark at 80% fewer active tokens.
  • thomaschill/unclog — Audits which MCP servers, skills and CLAUDE.md bloat are eating your context window.
  • ★ DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp — Indexes a codebase into a persistent knowledge graph so the agent stops re-reading everything.
  • ★ MemPalace/mempalace — Best-benchmarked open-source memory system, and free.
  • TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory — Team-level shared memory hub rather than per-developer memory.

RAG & Knowledge Graphs

Getting your own material into the model reliably.

  • ★ HKUDS/LightRAG — Simple, fast, graph-flavoured RAG. The default I'd start from.
  • HKUDS/RAG-Anything — All-in-one RAG framework from the same lab when LightRAG isn't enough.
  • ★ Graphify-Labs/graphify — Turns a codebase plus its docs, schemas and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph.
  • vitali87/code-graph-rag — RAG aimed squarely at multi-language monorepos.
  • ★ tirth8205/code-review-graph — Local-first persistent map of your codebase, exposed over MCP and CLI.
  • langchain-ai/openwiki — Writes and then maintains agent-facing docs for your repo.
  • pgvector/pgvector — Vectors inside Postgres. Usually the right answer before you buy a vector DB.
  • Chroma — Easiest local vector store to get running in an afternoon.

Second Brain & Notes

Where the knowledge lives when it isn't code.

  • ★ Obsidian — Plain markdown on your disk. That's exactly why agents work well against it.
  • kepano/obsidian-skills — Teaches your agent the Obsidian CLI and open formats. From Obsidian's own CEO.
  • ★ AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian — Self-organising second brain — drop any source in and it files itself.
  • ★ NotebookLM — Best free tool for interrogating a pile of sources you didn't write.
  • ★ teng-lin/notebooklm-py — Unofficial Python API + skill. Gets you features the web UI doesn't expose.
  • pjeby/hot-reload — Auto-reloads Obsidian plugins while you build them. Tiny, essential.

Research & Intelligence

Finding out what's actually true and actually current.

  • ★ mvanhorn/last30days-skill — Researches a topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN and Polymarket. My most-used research skill.
  • Panniantong/Agent-Reach — Gives the agent eyes on Twitter, Reddit and YouTube instead of guessing.
  • ★ Firecrawl — Search and scrape the live web at scale, in a format models can read.
  • firecrawl/anydoc — Word, PowerPoint, Excel, EPUB, PDF → clean Markdown.
  • ★ baidu/Unlimited-OCR — One-shot parsing of very long documents. Good where normal OCR falls over.
  • karpathy/autoresearch — Agents running their own research loop. Worth reading even if you never run it.
  • koala73/worldmonitor — Real-time news and geopolitical dashboard, AI-aggregated.
  • HKUDS/DeepTutor — Personalised tutoring that persists across sessions.
  • every-app/open-seo — Open-source answer to Semrush and Ahrefs.

Skill & Plugin Collections

Don't write a skill before checking whether someone already did.

  • obra/superpowers — The biggest agentic-skills framework going, plus an opinionated methodology.
  • ★ mattpocock/skills — Straight out of Matt Pocock's .agents directory. Heavy TypeScript bias, high quality.
  • addyosmani/agent-skills — Production-grade engineering skills from Addy Osmani.
  • garrytan/gstack — Garry Tan's literal Claude Code setup — 23 opinionated tools wired as a team.
  • affaan-m/ECC — Harness performance system: skills, instincts, memory, security in one bundle.
  • ★ HKUDS/OpenSpace — A management layer once you have too many skills to keep straight.
  • rohitg00/awesome-claude-code-toolkit — 135 agents, 35 skills, 42 commands in one place.
  • phuryn/pm-skills — Product-management skills — discovery through strategy. Not everything is code.
  • coreyhaines31/marketingskills — CRO, copywriting, SEO and growth skills.
  • slavingia/skills — Sahil Lavingia's skills, built around The Minimalist Entrepreneur.
  • Shubhamsaboo/awesome-llm-apps — 100+ agent and RAG apps you can read as worked examples.
  • anthropics/claude-cookbooks — Official notebooks. The fastest way to learn a technique properly.

Learning & Guides

Send these to someone who just installed Claude Code and is staring at a blinking cursor.

  • luongnv89/claude-howto — Visual, example-driven, basics to advanced agents. Best first stop.
  • FlorianBruniaux/claude-code-ultimate-guide — The most complete single guide: workflows, hooks, skills, MCP.
  • microsoft/AI-For-Beginners — 12 weeks, 24 lessons. Actual fundamentals, not prompt tricks.
  • asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks — Extracted system prompts. Read them to see how the pros really write instructions.

Agents & Orchestration

Running more than one agent without losing the plot.

  • msitarzewski/agency-agents — A whole agency of role-specialised agents, frontend through community.
  • stablyai/orca — An IDE for driving a fleet of parallel agents, whichever harness you use.
  • openai/codex-plugin-cc — Call Codex from inside Claude Code for reviews and delegated tasks. Two models beat one.
  • manaflow-ai/cmux — Terminal built for running several coding agents at once.
  • yc-software/qm — Multiplayer agent harness — built for teams, not solo runs.
  • ★ HKUDS/ClawTeam — Agent swarm behind a single command.
  • ★ gsd-build/gsd-2 — Meta-prompting and spec-driven development. Good if you like a rigid process.
  • louislva/claude-peers-mcp — Lets your separate Claude Code instances talk to each other.
  • vercel/eve — Vercel's open framework for building agents.
  • ★ chaseai-yt/grill-me-codex — Mine. Interviews you until the plan is airtight, then makes Codex attack it before you build.

Models, Routing & Cost

Picking the right model and not overpaying for it.

  • ★ OpenRouter — One API key, most models. Easiest way to A/B a model without a new account.
  • Artificial Analysis — Independent speed, cost and quality benchmarks. Check before believing a launch post.
  • LLM-Stats — Fast side-by-side of price and context window.
  • diegosouzapw/OmniRoute — MIT-licensed gateway: 330+ providers, 1200+ models, many free.
  • musistudio/claude-code-router — One local control plane to route Claude Code across different models.
  • BerriAI/litellm — The proxy layer most production stacks end up using.
  • AlexsJones/llmfit — One command tells you which models your actual hardware can run.
  • ★ Ollama — Local models with the least ceremony.
  • LM Studio — Ollama with a GUI. Better for people who don't live in a terminal.
  • JustVugg/colibri — Runs frontier MoE models on hardware you already own. Pure C, zero deps.

CLI & Terminal

Agents are best at things that have a command line. This is how you give them one.

  • ★ HKUDS/CLI-Anything — Makes any software agent-native by giving it a CLI. The big idea on this whole page.
  • ★ jackwener/OpenCLI — Turns any website into a CLI, using your already-logged-in browser.
  • ★ googleworkspace/cli — One command for Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Sheets and Docs. Official.
  • iOfficeAI/OfficeCLI — Office suite built so agents can read and edit documents directly.
  • ★ herdrdev/herdr — A runtime for your coding agents to actually live on.
  • ★ cli/cli — GitHub's own CLI. PRs, issues, releases, Actions — all scriptable by an agent.
  • anthropics/anthropic-cli — Official CLI for the Claude API. Handy for quick scripted calls.
  • junegunn/fzf — Fuzzy finder. Rewires how you use a terminal within a day.
  • BurntSushi/ripgrep — The fast grep. Already what your agent reaches for under the hood.
  • jesseduffield/lazygit — Git you can actually see. Best way to review what an agent just committed.
  • ★ sharkdp/bat — cat with syntax highlighting and line numbers.
  • yt-dlp/yt-dlp — Downloads audio and video from nearly anywhere. Backbone of most video pipelines.

Browser & Web Automation

Letting the agent drive a real browser.

  • ★ Playwright — The automation library to standardise on. Screenshots, forms, scraping, tests.
  • ★ microsoft/playwright-cli — Record actions and get generated Playwright code back.
  • browser-use/browser-harness — Self-healing harness so LLM web tasks survive a changed selector.
  • alibaba/page-agent — In-page GUI agent — drive a web interface in natural language.
  • ★ JCodesMore/ai-website-cloner-template — Clone any site with one command. Great for studying a layout you like.
  • ShawnPana/phone-harness — Lets an agent control your actual phone.

Deployment & Infrastructure

Getting it off your laptop.

  • ★ Vercel — Fastest path to a live frontend. The CLI is fully agent-drivable.
  • ★ Railway — Where I put things that need a real backend and a database.
  • ★ Supabase — Postgres, auth, storage and vectors. Usually the whole backend.
  • supabase/supabase — Self-host it if you'd rather not rent it.
  • Netlify — The other obvious static/edge host.
  • Fly.io — Containers close to your users, without a Kubernetes hobby.
  • ★ Docker — Still the unit of "works on my machine" being false.
  • apple/container — Linux containers on Apple silicon via lightweight VMs. Fast.
  • anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime — Filesystem and network limits on agent-run code. Read this before you go autonomous.
  • anthropics/claude-code-action — Runs Claude Code inside GitHub Actions.

Security & Code Review

The part people skip right up until they can't.

  • usestrix/strix — Open-source AI pentesting against your own app. Finds and helps fix.
  • alibaba/open-code-review — Battle-tested at Alibaba scale. Hybrid static + model review.
  • anthropics/defending-code-reference-harness — Threat modelling, scanning, triage and patching skills from Anthropic.

Video, Audio & Content

Turning work into something people can watch.

  • calesthio/OpenMontage — Agentic video production — 12 pipelines, 100+ operations.
  • ★ bradautomates/claude-video — /watch downloads a video, pulls frames and transcribes it. Claude can finally see video.
  • ★ Higgsfield — Image and video generation I use for covers and B-roll.
  • ★ Remotion — Video as React components. Programmatic, diffable, repeatable.
  • ★ diffusionstudio/lottie — Production-ready Lottie animations straight out of Claude Code or Codex.
  • op7418/guizang-ppt-skill — Genuinely good-looking HTML slide decks — editorial and Swiss layouts.
  • ElevenLabs — Voiceover that doesn't sound like 2023.
  • Zackriya-Solutions/meetily — Privacy-first meeting notes. Live transcription, runs locally.
  • ★ img2threejs/img2threejs — Reference image → animation-ready procedural Three.js. Genuinely surprising.
  • ★ oso95/scroll-world — Turns a brand into a scrollable 3D world landing page.

Voice & Dictation

Talking to your machine is roughly 3x faster than typing at it.

  • ★ bubnyukab/whisperflow-windows — Local, offline Wispr Flow alternative for Windows. Free, no account.
  • ★ drajb/whisper-local — Offline dictation for Windows and macOS. Small project, does the job.
  • huggingface/speech-to-speech — Build a local voice agent from open models.

Work, Career & Ops

Agents pointed at things that aren't code.

  • ★ paperclipai/paperclip — Managing agents as actual coworkers. Open source.
  • ★ santifer/career-ops — Scans job boards and grades listings against a structured A-F rubric.
  • MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search — The same idea, running entirely on your machine.
  • interviewstreet/hiring-agent — Scores resumes. Useful from either side of the table.
  • ★ n8n — Self-hostable automation. The glue when a skill isn't the right shape.
  • Composio — Pre-built tool integrations so you don't write another OAuth flow.

Editors & Harnesses

Where you sit while the agent works.

  • ★ Cursor — The IDE most people arrive from. Still excellent at inline edits.
  • Zed — Very fast, collaborative, increasingly agent-native.
  • ★ openai/codex — OpenAI's terminal agent. Best used as a second opinion on Claude's work.
  • xai-org/grok-build — xAI's harness and TUI. Fullscreen, mouse-interactive, extensible.
  • Warp — Terminal with agent features baked in rather than bolted on.
